//: Optional settings file for midpoint-mcp-server. Point MIDPOINT_MCP_CONFIG at it.
//credentials: NEVER put credentials here — they are read from the environment only.
//behavior: Every key below is optional; the values shown are the defaults.

identity.//credentialIsShared: Set true when MIDPOINT_USERNAME is a technical/shared account rather than one person's login. Self-scoped tools (list_my_team, list_my_teammates, list_my_managers, list_work_items, list_my_requests) then refuse in personal mode instead of answering for the service account. They still work for requests carrying a mapped end user (resource-server mode). whoami always answers, so a caller can see why.

team.//orgSource: Where a caller's org links come from: 'parentOrgRef' (midPoint's computed membership, the default), 'assignment' (org assignments only), 'fallback' (parentOrgRef, then assignments when it is empty), or 'both'.
team.//managerRelation: Relation local part marking a user as manager of an org. Local part only — 'manager', not 'org:manager'.
team.//memberRelation: Relation local part marking plain membership, used when searching an org for members.
team.//orgOids: Narrow which of the caller's orgs count as their team. Empty = all of them, which for a user in several orgs makes list_my_teammates return everyone in all of them.
team.//orgNames: Same, by org name (matched case-insensitively). Combined with orgOids as an OR.

requests.//requireRequestable: Refuse request_role for roles midPoint's catalog does not flag requestable. On by default: request_role submits a plain assignment-add, which midPoint turns into an approval case only where policy says so and otherwise executes immediately — so without this, 'request' is an unrestricted grant path. Use assign_role for a deliberate grant.
